description:
Problem. Leader sessions in feature delivery mode repeatedly stop to ask the owner whether their subagents may be batch members. `docs/agent/batch-feature-delivery.md` forbids a member from running as a subagent of its leader because a subagent shares the leader's tractable identity, but it names no other way to start a member, and a subagent is the only parallel dispatch a leader has. The same ban is repeated in the todo skill and implied by a `batch-land` refusal message.

Evidence (2026-11-12). A subagent reported the same worker id as its parent and all tracker write tools. `batch-land` already refuses any tracker write on a member item before landing except `take`, `release`, `renew`, `recover` and a `prepare` recorded in the integration log, whatever the identity. The audit in PR #3957 found no member tracker writes in four batches; the incident behind the rule was parallel leaders sharing one session. The tractable server states that claims are cooperative, not access control, and that a worker holds one claim per active batch.

Owner decisions (2026-11-12).
1. A member may run as a subagent of its own leader. The dispatch prompt must forbid tracker writes and require absolute worktree paths. The doc states the residual risk: a member `take` or `prepare` under the shared identity is not detected.
2. Delivery is one feature branch and one BenchBox pull request built by one session, not a registered batch.
3. The skill catalog (`joeharris76/skill-sync-skills`) is corrected and merged first; the BenchBox pull request then pins the merged commit and regenerates mirrors.
4. The catalog's global pin (`deployment/global/skill-sync.conf`) is bumped in a follow-up catalog pull request.

Order. (a) batch-member-subagent-skill-text-20261112: catalog text pull request, merge, then global-pin pull request. (b) One BenchBox branch carrying batch-member-subagent-doc-rule-20261112, batch-member-subagent-land-message-20261112 and batch-member-subagent-skill-pin-20261112. The BenchBox pull request is titled as a `docs(agent)` change, gets a self-review with every Critical and Required finding fixed, `make pr-preflight`, `make pr-open`, then `make pr-arm` and is followed to merge; a real CI failure is fixed and pushed, a spurious ejection re-armed. (c) After the BenchBox pull request merges: finish this item, then take and finish each member.

Out of scope, by decision: a launch command printed by `batch-member-create`, a stricter `take` check in `batch-land`, and any tractable change.

Guardrails (all items under this umbrella):
- No edit, branch or commit in the primary clone. Work in a worktree made with `make worktree-create`, run `make agent-write-preflight`, and pass absolute worktree paths to every file tool.
- Never hand-edit `.claude/skills` or `.agents/skills`; mirrors change only through `make skill-sync`.
- Do not register a batch: this work changes the batch loop, which is always delivered serially.
- Do not change guard behaviour in `scripts/batch_integration.py` (`LEADER_MEMBER_OPS`, `member_tracker_writes`, `_check_member_writes` window and exemptions). Only the refusal wording changes.
- Keep the rule that leaders do not share a session or identity with another leader.
- Do not write to `~/.claude/skills`, `~/.codex/skills`, `~/.agents/skills` or `~/.skill-sync-deployment`. Activating global loaders is a separately approved owner action.
- Check the commit identity and its config origin before the first commit in each repository; add no agent attribution.
- Stop and report, without working around it, on: a failed gate that needs an owner-only action, a hold label, an unresolved Critical or High review finding, or any decision gate below that says stop.
